prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of 2010 UK manifesto proposals (ideology-free, no names)

- Tax and benefits: Raise the personal income tax allowance to £10,000, removing 3.6m low earners from income tax and cutting most workers’ bills by about £700; fund via restricting higher-rate pension tax relief, aligning capital gains tax with income tax, anti-avoidance measures, a per‑plane aviation duty (higher for domestic flights with viable alternatives), and a 1% levy on property value above £2m. Reform non‑dom status (limited to seven years). Restore the state pension link to earnings with a triple guarantee (earnings, prices, or 2.5%).

- Deficit and spending: Identify multi‑year savings (e.g., £400 public‑sector pay-rise cap for two years, restrict tax credits, end Child Trust Fund payments, scrap ID cards, cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B, prison reform, scale back central inspection regimes). Establish a cross‑party Council on Financial Stability and conduct a full spending review.

- Economy and finance: Separate retail and investment banking; introduce a bank levy until separation is complete; reform bonuses; require state‑influenced banks to lend to viable firms. Create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges. Launch a one‑year jobs and green stimulus (shipyard upgrades for offshore wind, “eco cash‑back” for home efficiency, public‑building retrofits, bring 250,000 empty homes into use, bus scrappage). Establish a UK Infrastructure Bank to leverage private capital for transport and energy.

- Business and mutuals: Reduce unnecessary regulation with sunset clauses and a “one‑in, one‑out” rule; stop over‑implementation of EU rules; shift business rates to site values under local control; refocus or replace Regional Development Agencies; restore a public‑interest test for takeovers and reintroduce the Operating and Financial Review. Support co‑ops, mutuals, and social enterprises; separate Post Office from Royal Mail (retain Post Office in public ownership; partial Royal Mail sale with employee trust stake).

- Science and work: Protect the science budget’s integrity; expand open access to publicly funded research; base funding on peer review; safeguard adviser independence. Extend the right to request flexible working; require name‑blind recruitment and pay audits for larger firms; improve disability employment support.

- Education and skills: Introduce a £2.5bn Pupil Premium targeted at disadvantaged pupils; reduce class sizes; guarantee SEN assessment at age five; improve teacher training; tackle bullying. Replace the National Curriculum with a minimum entitlement; scale back Key Stage 2 tests; create a General Diploma integrating academic and vocational routes; allow 14–19 study at colleges; reform league tables. Phase out university tuition fees over six years (final‑year fees scrapped immediately); create a National Bursary Scheme; expand foundation degrees and adult apprenticeships; end Train to Gain for large firms.

- Health and care: Cut NHS bureaucracy (halve Department of Health; abolish Strategic Health Authorities), reinvest in cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia, and prevention; integrate health and social care; guaranteed respite for full‑time carers; expand talking therapies; tighten alcohol pricing policies; improve air quality. Introduce treatment time entitlements; elected Local Health Boards to replace PCT boards; greater GP choice and access; duty of candour on medical errors; stricter clinician language/competence tests.

- Culture and media: Maintain free national museums; seed a Creative Enterprise Fund; ease small‑venue live music rules; reform Lottery tax; use dormant betting accounts for local sport; protect playing fields; safeguard BBC independence; support local media.

- Families and consumers: Shared parental leave; fathers’ antenatal leave; extend flexible working. Incorporate the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child into law; publish anonymised Serious Case Reviews; strengthen youth services; equal minimum wage over 16 (except apprentices). Progressive energy tariffs and social tariffs; fairer water charges; cap unfair bank fees; create PostBank; consider caps on credit-card rates; improve consumer service standards; cut regulated rail fares in real terms; refund rules for rail‑replacement buses; regulate private clamping.

- Climate and environment: Target a zero‑carbon economy by 2050; over 40% emissions cut by 2020 vs 1990; 40% zero‑carbon electricity by 2020 (moving to 100% by 2050), prioritising marine/offshore sources; renewables roadmap; European Supergrid; large‑scale home insulation; block new unabated coal; oppose new nuclear; strengthen efficiency schemes. Lead EU action to tighten ETS, curb HFCs, and fund adaptation. Protect forests; ban illegal timber imports; develop product eco‑labelling.

- International development and finance: Legislate to reach 0.7% of GNI for aid by 2013; explore financial transaction taxes and aviation/shipping carbon markets; reform IFIs; curb corruption and tax havens; support health, education, clean water, social protection, debt cancellation, and anti‑vulture measures.

- Defence and foreign policy: Immediate Strategic Security and Defence Review; no like‑for‑like Trident replacement; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; deepen European defence cooperation; raise lower ranks’ pay; speed family‑housing upgrades. Support EU coordination on major foreign policy issues; arms‑trade controls; inquiry into alleged complicity in torture/rendition; two‑state solution for the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict; diplomatic approach to Iran; conditions‑based strategy in Afghanistan to enable drawdown.

- Policing and justice: Fund 3,000 additional police; cut paperwork; directly elect police authorities with stronger powers; create a National Crime Reduction Agency; share anonymised hospital data to target violence; “stop‑on‑request” for night buses; better hate‑crime recording. Presumption against short prison sentences; expand restorative justice and neighbourhood panels; require prisoner work with victim compensation; divert addicts and the mentally ill to appropriate settings; cancel new prison building.

- Immigration and asylum: Reintroduce exit checks; create a National Border Force with police powers; regional points‑based work system; tougher enforcement against rogue employers; prioritise deporting serious offenders; earned citizenship for long‑term, law‑abiding residents under set criteria. Establish an independent asylum agency; coordinate at EU level; allow asylum seekers to work; end child detention; use alternatives to detention; ban removals to persecution risk.

- Housing and transport: Make repossession a last resort; bring empty homes into use; scale up home insulation; tighten new‑build efficiency; enable councils to build and retain revenues; scrap Home Information Packs (retain EPCs). Shift investment from major roads to rail reopenings and capacity; regulate buses locally; expand safe cycling/walking; per‑plane aviation duty, higher for substitutable domestic routes; cancel Heathrow third runway and other South East expansions; prepare revenue‑neutral road pricing in a later parliament; rural fuel discount.

- Rural and environment management: Expand access to the countryside; return major planning decisions locally; third‑party right of appeal; zero‑waste strategy with more recycling and anaerobic digestion; restore biodiversity by 2020; equalise VAT on repair vs new‑build; elect parts of National Park boards; new community green designations; double woodland by 2050; treat gardens as greenfield in planning. Improve flood and water management; smart meters in shortage areas.

- Rural communities and farming: Allow higher council tax on second homes and require planning permission where needed; protect rural post offices; promote affordable rural housing; refund VAT to mountain rescue. Create a statutory supermarket code with an independent regulator; rebalance Single Farm Payments toward working and hill farmers; support farm biogas and apprenticeships; push CAP reform; improve origin and sustainability labelling; use public procurement to expand sustainable and fair‑trade markets.

- Voluntary sector: “Easy giving” accounts at state‑owned banks; single‑rate Gift Aid; portable criminal records checks for volunteers.

- Political and constitutional reform: Proportional representation (STV) for MPs with a smaller Commons; votes at 16; fixed‑term parliaments; stronger Commons scrutiny and control of its timetable; replace the Lords with a fully elected chamber; written constitution via a citizens’ convention and referendum; extend FOI to monopoly public‑service providers; stronger data protection. Recall MPs for serious wrongdoing; £10,000 cap on donations; tighter lobbying rules and transparency; tax‑residency rules for officeholders and candidates. Proportional voting for local elections; pilot Local Income Tax to replace council tax; return business rates to councils on site values; devolve funding powers; elected police authorities and health boards; scrap regional Whitehall tiers. Implement further devolution to Scotland and Wales; replace the Barnett formula with a needs‑based system; address England’s status via a constitutional convention.

- Civil liberties and security: Introduce a Freedom Bill (regulate CCTV and local surveillance; fairer extradition rules; protect jury trial; parental consent for school fingerprinting); restore protest rights; reform libel law; scrap ID cards and biometric passport plans; halt blanket retention of communications data; remove innocent people’s DNA; protect the Human Rights Act; scrap the ContactPoint database. Counter‑terrorism reforms: end control orders; reduce pre‑charge detention to 14 days; allow intercept evidence; expand post‑charge questioning; strengthen community engagement.
